chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yasar from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Durust from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When the beast stumbles under the man and he says to it 'May you be cursed' (Ta'asti), it says 'May the bones of our Lord be cursed' (Ta'asa a'sana al-Rabb)."
ai.seo_question: What does the animal say when a person says 'Ta'asti' to it?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on tethering horses, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual consequence of cursing one's mount, linking the animal's response to the owner's intent. It serves as a practical ethical guideline for travelers, warning that careless speech towards creation can result in the owner bearing the curse, thereby emphasizing mindfulness (*muraqabah*) in daily interactions with animals.
